anomalies.observed: D1 is a 12 V zener with its cathode on /NET0058, the T8 gate node, and its anode on GND. R14 pulls that gate node toward /+24V_F, which is also T8's source. With T1 off, D1 clamps the gate near 12 V while the source is near 24 V, leaving T8 with about -12 V gate-to-source bias.
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel MOSFET that should turn off when T1 is inactive, its gate should rise to the source voltage. Any gate-protection zener should clamp gate-to-source voltage, not clamp the gate to ground in a way that leaves the MOSFET turned on.
anomalies.impact: T8 remains biased on even when T1 is off, so the gate control cannot reliably disable the +24 V feed through T8; the downstream rail may remain powered when it is supposed to be switched off.

parsed.summary: The zener D1 clamps the P-channel T8 gate to ground rather than to its source. This leaves T8 with a strongly negative gate-to-source voltage in the nominal off state, defeating the gate pull-up and likely preventing the +24 V feed from being switched off.
